definitions.explanation: Something offered to a deity, spirit, or respected person as a gift of devotion, gratitude, or sacrifice.

examples.japanese: {神|かみ}への{捧|ささ}げ{物|もの}を{用意|ようい}した。
examples.english: I prepared an offering for the gods.

examples.japanese: {祭壇|さいだん}に{捧|ささ}げ{物|もの}が{並|なら}べられていた。
examples.english: Offerings were arranged on the altar.

examples.japanese: この{作品|さくひん}は{亡|な}き{師匠|ししょう}への{捧|ささ}げ{物|もの}として{書|か}かれた。
examples.english: This work was written as a tribute to the late master.

notes:
Composed of {捧|ささ}げる (to offer; to dedicate) + {物|もの} (thing). Used in both religious and secular contexts. In religious usage, it refers to physical offerings placed at altars or shrines. In secular usage, it can refer to a creative work, performance, or gesture dedicated to someone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神|かみ}への{捧|ささ}げ{物|もの}: offering to the gods
- {祭壇|さいだん}の{捧|ささ}げ{物|もの}: altar offering
- {捧|ささ}げ{物|もの}をする: to make an offering

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {供|そな}え{物|もの}: offering (at a shrine, grave, or altar) — the more common everyday word for offerings placed at Buddhist altars or graves
- {貢|みつ}ぎ{物|もの}: tribute — specifically something given to a superior or ruler, often implying obligation
- {奉納|ほうのう}{品|ひん}: votive offering — a formal offering dedicated to a shrine or temple
